bull.b: The large recurring component ties revenue to the installed base and procedure utilization rather than only new system sales. Continued instrument, accessory and service growth can support durable cash generation as customers perform more procedures over time.

A growing global installed base broadens Intuitive’s clinical footprint and creates additional opportunities for procedure-linked purchases and service revenue. Expansion across more than 70 countries also strengthens customer familiarity and supports future utilization growth.

An essentially debt-free balance sheet and strong operating cash flow provide substantial flexibility to fund research, product development, global expansion and capital returns. This financial capacity can help the company sustain investment while absorbing operating volatility.

bear.b: Lower revenue per procedure creates a structural headwind for the recurring consumables model even if procedure volumes continue growing. The pressure may persist as China pricing changes and extended-life instruments roll out across countries through 2027.

Slower U.S. procedure growth and difficult Chinese operating conditions could moderate utilization and system placement momentum in important markets. These regional pressures may make consolidated growth more dependent on international expansion and newer procedure categories.

The settlement demonstrates a meaningful legal cost, while higher compensation, headcount and prototype spending are raising the operating cost base. Continued expense growth could limit near-term earnings conversion even as revenue and non-GAAP profitability remain strong.
